findings.text: follow-on: the delivered head adds a failure the base arm does not have. tests/test_a_pane_settles_when_no_work_is_live.py::test_the_real_follower_settles_when_the_host_advertises_it fails at head both in the 46-file importer suite (logs/after-importers.log) and in the isolated three-file run (logs/head-disputed-isolated.log, 2 failed / 66 passed), while the same file passes at base in isolation (logs/base-pane-isolated.log, 11 passed). The test spawns a real follower subprocess and asserts it delivered rows; it does not reference checkout_trust, source_code_identity, follower_code_stamp or materialize_committed_tree, and the early return added at reckon/crew_follow_* triggers only on IDENTITY_UNKNOWN, which a healthy git checkout does not produce. Attribution therefore reads as contention rather than as this change, but it is unresolved: it reproduces at head and not at base in isolation, so it must not be promoted past without the coordinator's own check.

follow-on: the node's done_when requires the importer suite to add no failure against base, and the recorded arms add two (added_failure_count above). The node reported them under follow_ons rather than triaging them, which its fence ('a failure outside this node's declared scope is reported under follow_ons rather than triaged or fixed') directs; the measure is nevertheless not literally met and the coordinator owns the attribution before promotion.
